engine.meaning: Every sentence of the original is kept almost word for word: "she sets it aside and picks the next one", "I'll start out playing without a queen", "he is learning both to win and lose graciously". Nothing lost or added.

engine.tone: The earnest, reflective parent-forum tone is intact because the text is intact: "Is this a legitimate concern at his age".
engine.flow: Reads as the original does; the only seam is "My concern, which I expressed to my missus", where slang drops into a formal clause.
engine.variety: Only a handful of swaps, and "littlie" is used twice ("let a littlie win", "keep your littlie happy").
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, question and answer in full: "stacking the deck in his favour", "playing without a queen".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points survive: the dealer trick ("she puts it aside and picks the next one"), the tiles buried "right at the bottom on purpose", the chess handicap, the stepdad, the article. "or they won't stay keen enough to keep playing" keeps the adult as the one losing interest.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "having a squiz at the tiles" for looking, "over the moon" for ecstatic, "win fair and square" for legitimately, "What bugs me" for my concern.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian parent posting: "I reckon that's spot on.", "Thing is,", "I dunno if she doesn't notice", "cos he knew I hadn't just handed it to him". Nothing forced.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light, even touch across the text: "squiz", "reckon", "missus", "keen", "cos", "mum". Right for level 2, no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Stays a thoughtful parenting question and a measured reply: "Is that a fair worry at his age", "he's learning to win and lose with good grace".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "He loves a game, but he seems (to me, anyway) more interested in the playing than the winning." One slightly flat line: "went and put every tile".
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied, light choices; "cos" appears twice ("cos he knew", "cos they're not equipped") and "reckon" twice.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Recognisably the same post and answer, its shape and examples intact: "I'll start out playing without a queen, but still do my best to win."

yarn-troppo.meaning: Keeps every point, with asides: "Talk about a card sharp." reacts to the cheating (colour), "(she's the dealer, naturally)" adds a small flourish. "keep turning up to the table" elaborates 'continue playing'.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly exact: "pulled her up on it", "off with the fairies" for distracted, "cop a disappointment". "I don't want him rocking up expecting to win" strains: 'rock up' means arrive, not approach a game with expectations.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Strongly natural Aussie voice: "Then last night I twigged", "went the whole hog", "it fair takes the fun out of it", "Dunno if she doesn't notice". A couple of lines lean on stock phrase: "handed it to him on a plate".
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 2: "Every. Single. Time.", "went the whole hog", "Talk about a card sharp.", "off with the fairies", "rocking up", "cop a disappointment". Reads closer to a level 3 yarn; no swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The original's measured worry gets a punchier, more comic edge ("he wins. Every. Single. Time.", "Talk about a card sharp.") but the earnest question still lands: "Is that a fair worry at his age?"
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable: "Once the deck's stacked against you, the fun goes out the window." Some lines run a little busy: "she starts sneaking a squiz at the tiles to see if the next one off the top (she's the dealer, naturally) would be the winner".
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range with little repeated: "twigged", "squiz", "whole hog", "card sharp", "pulled her up", "gutted", "heap more", "cop". 'win' as a noun recurs ("a real long-term win for him") but that is the subject.
yarn-troppo.essence: Still the same question and answer, all examples kept: "I'll start out without my queen, but still give it everything I've got."

dinkum-3.meaning: All points survive: "she pops it to one side and picks the next one", "she'd gone and put every tile that matched her card right down the bottom on purpose", chess without the queen, the stepdad, the article. "I told her this" keeps 'which I expressed to my wife'.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "Chrissie" for Christmas, "have a red-hot go at winning" for 'still do my best to win', "off with the fairies" for distracted. "being spewin' when he doesn't" is a little strong for 'disappointed' (spewing is angry or gutted) but works.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural: "Turns out the missus has literally been stacking the deck for him", "He loves a game", "I dunno if she doesn't notice". "I've just had the exact opposite go of it" is a slightly forced construction.
dinkum-3.register: A touch above level 2 in places ("spewin'", "Chrissie", "red-hot go", "off with the fairies") but mostly light: "squiz", "reckon", "keen".
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the reflective question and measured reply: "Is that a fair worry at his age?", "he's learning to win and lose like a good sport".
dinkum-3.flow: Mostly smooth; a few clunky joins: "I've just had the exact opposite go of it with my five-year-old son.", "luck mostly counts for heaps more than strategy", "a win's a real achievement for either of us, and watching my handicap shrink over time will be a real long-term achievement for him" repeats 'real ... achievement'.
dinkum-3.variety: Good spread ("squiz", "pops", "spewin'", "Chrissie", "red-hot go", "heaps"), with "real achievement" / "real long-term achievement" and "cos" twice.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the original, retold: "Say, when he learns chess, I'll start out without my queen".

unharnessed.meaning: Every point kept: "she pops it aside and picks the next one", "put all the tiles that matched her card right at the bottom on purpose", the chess handicap, the stepdad, the article. "so they stay keen enough to keep playing" keeps the adult's interest.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "having a squiz at the tiles", "the deck was being fiddled" for manipulated, "be gutted when he doesn't" for disappointed, "win fair and square".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural and unforced: "I reckon that's spot on.", "Turns out my wife has literally been stacking the deck", "give it my best shot". Some phrasing stays close to the original's formality: "an easy, age-appropriate matching game", "I made a deliberate decision".
unharnessed.register: A light touch that fits level 2: "squiz", "reckon", "gutted", "keen", "pops it aside", "favour"; keeps "Should you let a toddler win?" plain. Perhaps a shade light in the reply half.
unharnessed.tone: The calm, earnest parent voice and the measured reply both come through: "Is that a fair worry at his age", "he's learning to win and lose like a good sport".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth and clean: "When the deck's stacked against you, it stops being fun." Only "a real achievement for either of us ... a real long-term achievement for him" repeats.
unharnessed.variety: Varied light terms without tics; "real achievement" repeats once, as in the original's 'real accomplishment'.
unharnessed.essence: Plainly the original, retold lightly: "For example, when he learns chess I'll start off playing without a queen".
